title: The first Moscow show trial
gist: A short culture notebook covering three unrelated items: Sergei Loznitsa's 2018 documentary on the 1930 Moscow trial that presaged Stalin's Great Purge, a newly translated 1946 Éric Rohmer novel, and a new recording of Brahms' three violin sonatas.

insights.claim: A 1930 Moscow trial that falsely accused several leading economists and engineers of conspiring in a coup d'état served as the harbinger of Stalin's later show trials, including the 1936 Trial of the Sixteen, in which every defendant, including Grigory Zinoviev and Lev Kamenev, was shot on 24 August 1936 after tortured confessions.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Historical marker of how Soviet show-trial machinery escalated from targeting technical/economic elites in 1930 to top political rivals by 1936 — a template for recognizing early-stage purge patterns in authoritarian regimes.
insights.quote: It is 90 years this month since the Trial of the Sixteen, which commenced Stalin’s Great Purge of veteran Bolshevik rivals, among whom Grigory Zinoviev and Lev Kamenev were the most prominent.

insights.claim: Ukrainian filmmaker Sergei Loznitsa's 2018 documentary 'The Trial' uses restored archival footage of the 1930 Moscow trial, capturing the visible enthusiasm of the courtroom crowd as especially chilling.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Points to a specific archival documentary resource for understanding the visual/propaganda mechanics of Stalin-era show trials.
insights.quote: The pristine footage makes for grim but compelling viewing, the joy unconfined on the faces of the mob especially chilling.

insights.claim: Filmmaker Éric Rohmer, known primarily as a director, also wrote a 1946 novel titled 'Élisabeth' under the pseudonym Gilbert Cordier — his only known novel — now translated into English by Aaron Kerner.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: A niche literary-history data point on a previously obscure early work by a major filmmaker, of interest to collectors/publishers of translated literary rediscoveries.
insights.quote: My love of the films of Éric Rohmer is well documented, but his career as a novelist seemed all but a rumour.
insights.locator: Second item, on Rohmer the novelist

insights.claim: Brahms composed his three violin sonatas over a ten-year period from 1878, and reportedly held back the third from publication because he was troubled by the sheer drama of its emotional range; a new recording by violinist Mark Kaplan and his son David has been released.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Notes a new classical recording release of interest to collectors of the Brahms violin sonata repertoire.
insights.quote: The composer held back the third from publication, perhaps because he was troubled by the sheer drama of its emotional range.
insights.locator: Third item, on Brahms' violin sonatas
